A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Adaptive Exploration for Multi-Reward Multi-Policy Evaluation. Their main text, equations, figures, notation table, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching material across changed pagination.

before.justification: v2 reports original tabular-MDP experiments comparing MR-NaS with other exploration methods in Figures 3–4 and 10–12, with experimental details in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments, including the main-text comparisons and appendix results across environment sizes and policy-evaluation scenarios.

M1.justification: The MR-NaS design is retained, but Equation (6) changes the denominator of U from 4ε² to 2ε², doubling Algorithm 1's stopping threshold for a fixed observation history. Appendix B.2.5 also removes the t ≥ 0 constraint from the reward-optimization linear program. These are limited procedural corrections.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Riverswim, Forked Riverswim, DoubleChain, and NArms under finite-reward multi-policy, reward-free multi-policy, and reward-free single-policy scenarios. No evaluated environment, reward coverage, or task scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership matches within each experiment. Figures 3/10 include SF-NR, GVFExplorer, and both Noisy Policy variants; Figures 4/11 omit GVFExplorer; Figure 12 compares MR-NaS with the two Noisy Policy variants. These memberships are identical across versions.

E3.justification: Appendices C.2–C.4 retain the environment parameters, target-policy and reward sampling, one-million-step budgets, empirical-model value evaluation, and 500-step MR-NaS optimization schedule. The theoretical stopping-rule correction does not establish a change to these fixed-budget experiments.

E4.justification: The Riverswim sensitivity analysis over transition probability, reward sets, and state-space size in Figure 5 is retained. The environment-size comparisons and single-policy results in Figures 10–12 also match; no ablation, robustness test, or supplementary empirical analysis is introduced.

E5.justification: Both versions report 30 seeds, shaded 95% confidence intervals, and bootstrap interval estimation in Appendix C.4. No repeated-run count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The result curves in Figures 3–5 and 10–12 are unchanged, as are their reported trends and the discussion of MR-NaS, SF-NR, and GVFExplorer. The changed mathematical bound constants are assessed under T1, rather than as empirical performance changes.

T1.justification: v3 adds uniform-policy aperiodicity, a confusing policy–reward pair at every state, and a unique interior optimal allocation through Assumptions 3.1, 4.3, and 5.1. It restricts Ω(M) to positive allocations and conditions the lower-bound theorem. Appendix B.2.1 substantially expands the stationary-flow, irreducibility, and density arguments; C.1 specifies additional proof conditions. The relaxed bound and its derivation receive a factor-of-two correction, alongside smaller mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The principal contributions—instance-dependent policy-evaluation bounds, a convex relaxation, and adapted MR-NaS—remain. The abstract softens the novelty statement from an uninvestigated setting to one not systematically studied, while the newly imposed assumptions qualify the scope of the theoretical guarantees.

C2.justification: v3 materially qualifies applicability: it removes the assertion that the results extend to weakly communicating MDPs, explains the aperiodicity requirement, and discusses excluded boundary or nonunique optimal allocations and possible remedies. Appendix B.2.1 newly explains why constraints on target-policy actions alone do not guarantee irreducibility. These limitations substantially refine how the guarantees should be interpreted; the empirical interpretations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.1 newly specifies a max(1, ...) safeguard in the forcing-policy temperature denominator, although C.3 retains the unguarded expression. Most added forcing-policy details already appear in v2's C.3. Experimental hyperparameters, CVXPY use, and repository access remain unchanged; the main-text README filename is corrected to match the existing appendix instruction.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jedra and Proutiere (2020) when discussing nonunique-allocation remedies and removes Grant et al. (2006) with the disciplined-convex-programming passage. It also adds a focused distinction from earlier best-policy-identification work concerning irreducibility. The broader related-work discussion is retained.

P1.justification: v3 makes local grammatical and terminology corrections, adds a notation paragraph, and organizes the expanded lower-bound proof into named stages. Some passages move, but the section hierarchy and most exposition remain intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 expands substantially with additional notation entries. Algorithm 1 changes column, and appendix algorithms and figures shift with text reflow. The existing plots retain their curves, axes, and legends; there is no broader visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 corrects the central relaxation's factor-of-two error and makes important assumptions and proof steps explicit, improving precision and checkability. The added qualifications appropriately narrow applicability, but the relaxation gap acknowledged in Section 4.3 remains unresolved, and forcing-policy formulas are not fully consistent between C.1 and C.3. The evidence supports a limited overall improvement.
